:::{.example #CLTExponential name="CLT and the gamma distribution"}
Consider taking iid samples $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ from a $\text{Gamma}(\alpha=2,\beta=1)$ distribution.
Then the MGF of each\ $X_i$ is
$$
  M_X(t) = (1-t)^{-2},
  \qquad t<1.
$$
Hence the MGF of the sample mean $\overline{X}$ is
$$
  M_{\overline{X}}(t) =
  \operatorname{E}\!\left[e^{t\overline{X}}\right]
  =
  \prod_{i=1}^n M_X\!\left(\frac{t}{n}\right)
  =
  \left(1-\frac{t}{n}\right)^{-2n}.
$$
This is the MGF of a $\text{Gamma}\!\left(\alpha = 2n,\ \beta = 1/n\right)$ distribution, so
$$
  \overline{X}
  \sim
  \text{Gamma}(2n,1/n).
$$
The sampling distribution (Fig.\ \@ref(fig:CLTDemoLatex)) becomes increasingly similar to a normal distribution as the sample size increases, and the approximation is reasonably good even for $n=10$.
:::



```{r, CLTDemoLatex, fig.align="center", echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Exact sampling distribution of the mean (solid lines) overlaid with the asymptotic CLT normal approximation (dashed lines). The samples are drawn from a Gamma$(\\alpha = 2, \\beta = 1)$ distribution. Note that the scale on the horizontal axis is different for the top three and bottom three plots.", out.width='100%', fig.width=7}
# Gamma(shape=2, scale=1): Xbar ~ Gamma(shape=n*alpha, scale=beta/n)
# mu = 2, sigma = sqrt(2)

###  Set up  ###
alpha <- 2
beta  <- 1
mu    <- alpha * beta
sg    <- sqrt(alpha) * beta

ns <- c(2, 10, 25, 50, 100)

x <- seq( max(mu - 5*sg, 1e-4), 
          mu + 5*sg, 
          length.out = 600)

###  Build x grid and densities for each n  ###
traces <- lapply(ns, function(n) {
  se   <- sg / sqrt(n)
  x    <- x
  yex  <- dgamma(x, 
                 shape = n * alpha, 
                 scale = beta/n)
  yclt <- dnorm(x,  
                mean  = mu,        
                sd   = se)
  list(x = x, 
       yex = yex, 
       yclt = yclt, 
       n = n)
})

###  Build figure  ###
par(mfrow = c(2, 3),
    mar = c(5.1, 3.1, 4.1, 1.1) ) # DEFAULT: 5.1 4.1 4.1 2.1

# GAMMA DISTN

plot(x = x, 
     y = dgamma(x, 
                shape = alpha, 
                scale = beta),
     type = "l",
     xlab = expression(italic(x)),
     ylab = "",
     axes = FALSE,
     main = "Distribution of the\nindividual observations",
     lwd = 2)
axis(side = 1)

### SAMPLING DISTNS
for (i in (1:length(ns))){
  plot(x = traces[[i]]$x, 
       y = traces[[i]]$yex,
       type = "l",
       xlab = expression(bar(italic(x))),
       ylab = "",
       axes = FALSE,
       xlim = if(i > 2) {c(0, 4)} else {c(0, max(x))},
       main = expression(bold(Sampling~distribution)),
       sub = bquote("(" * Sample~size~italic(n) == .(ns[i]) * ")"),
       lwd = 2)
  axis(side = 1)
  lines(x = traces[[i]]$x, 
        y = traces[[i]]$yclt,
        lty = 2,
        lwd = 2)
}
```
